question: Does the staged loader reach and register the Supervisor on the exact 3.1.32 firmware in Mirage?
prototype_hypothesis: Character-driver registration is the type-1 inode variant at 0xc4f7c40, not the type-7 variant at 0xc4e38ce.
callsite_evidence: Mirage firmware miwear.watch.n66cn_v3.1.32_full_489f2050; its vela_ap.bin SHA-256 is 9c02dab4020b2cc9666ee7d34cf27d311b76aadcec519a38361bbcbd94c53264, equal to the target.
Only the complete package mounts /system and the resource partition; importing vela_ap.bin alone leaves the panel black.
Installer face packaged by the patched Facetory lua-layer exporter at protocol 0x0800, package id 366140016; the n66 engine then runs /data/app/watchface/market/366140016/main.lua (miwear_lua_run).

Run executed stage0 (cave 0x200D0000), stage1 (Kmem stage2 image + MPU lease), stage2 (Supervisor ELF input in Kmem, resident image 149,866 B from Umem via memalign), constructor, and opened /dev/canopus.
CPC2 INSTALL 0, INSTALL 2, RESTORE_AFTER_BOOT, INSTALL 1 and INSTALL 2 all returned result 5; the installer displayed 'Run completed'.
/data/canopus/registry.bin is written with magic CDR1; the Supervisor persisted its registry after Manager registration.
control_flow_evidence: Stage2 skips an extra MPU lease for the Umem resident image: the privileged default map covers PSRAM as normal executable memory; the first MPU lease attempt failed with no free region (-310).
The v8 backend identity guard accepts NUL/LF/CR at the 3.1.32 build.prop token boundary.
The three inode registration siblings set types 1, 2 and 7; only type 1 makes /dev/canopus openable (types 2/7 made open return ENOSYS).
ownership_analysis: The Supervisor owns its Umem image and registry; the installer owns the staged files under /data/canopus. The Manager app and launcher entry were registered through app_install/app_launcher paths.
unsafe_assumptions: Emulator evidence only. No physical device probe; cache behaviour, MPU default-map execution and the Kmem/Umem split are not device-proven.
The v8 Manager page/launcher and notification service entries are only partially exercised (Run completed; module install/activate not run).
The Facetory Lua-layer patch is required to build the installer face.
recommended_probe: Repeat on a physical Band 9 3.1.32: Run, open the Manager from the launcher, install/enable/disable a module, and reboot with recovery.
